name: Champions Boat League & Vallam Kali
tagline: Kerala’s snake‑boat (vallam kali) season — CBL races across Alappuzha to Kollam (Sep–Nov 2026)
summary: Champions Boat League (CBL) packages Kerala’s traditional vallam kali into a state‑wide league. Season 6 runs across Alappuzha and Kollam venues from September 19 to November 21, 2026.
description: Champions Boat League (CBL) is Kerala Tourism’s franchise-style season of vallam kali (snake‑boat) races, staging weekend races at iconic backwater venues. The league presents traditional chundan valloms (snake boats) in timed heats and finals, turning local boat‑race rituals into a multi‑venue sporting circuit.

Vallam kali is a living cultural tradition tied to Onam and harvest‑season festivals; CBL packages that energy for visitors by scheduling races across Alappuzha district and finishing the season at Ashtamudi Lake in Kollam. The league draws large riverbank crowds, local pageantry and television coverage.

For visitors, CBL delivers a dramatic, close‑to‑water spectacle: long wooden chundan boats manned by dozens of oarsmen, rhythmic drum beats, boat processions and finish‑line sprints decided by seconds. The season runs in the autumn–early winter window, making it a convenient add‑on to Kerala backwater travel.
Confirm specific race dates and local arrangements before you travel; venues, start times and formal viewing areas change year to year and are posted by Kerala Tourism and local organisers.
highlights: Seasonal league format: multiple weekend races across Kerala (CBL Season 6: Sep 19–Nov 21, 2026).
Marquee venues in Alappuzha (Punnamada/Karuvatta/Pulinkunnu/Kainakary) and final at Ashtamudi Lake, Kollam.
Spectacle of chundan vallom (snake boats) — dozens of oarsmen, drum beats and tight finishes.
Local festival atmosphere: processions, temple ties, food stalls and large riverside crowds.
Good for photographers and cultural travellers; races are short, intense and timed to the millisecond.

sections.heading: Background
body: Vallam kali (literally 'boat play') is a traditional Kerala boat‑race practice tied to temple festivals and the Onam season. Modern high‑profile races such as the Nehru Trophy and the President’s Trophy have long been focal points for the sport.

Kerala Tourism launched the Champions Boat League in 2019 to present vallam kali as a season‑long sporting festival. CBL adapts the traditional format into an 11‑race league (Season 6 in 2026) with heats, finals and a points table across venues from Alappuzha to Kollam.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Arrive well before the scheduled start to watch the boat processions, team warmups and mass drills. Expect intense racing over short courses — each final can be decided by fractions of a second — and large crowds lining narrow banks and bridges.

Combine a race with backwater activities: take a short houseboat cruise before or after the event, explore nearby village markets, sample riverside snacks and watch boat sheds where the chundans are maintained. Respect the local viewing zones and follow instructions from event stewards.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best time: the CBL/vallam kali season runs in the autumn–early winter window; Season 6 dates in 2026 run from September 19 to November 21. Check the official schedule for the precise venue list and any last‑minute changes.

Practicalities: Alappuzha and nearby towns serve as primary bases for multiple races; Kollam (Ashtamudi Lake) hosts the season final. Expect large crowds, limited riverbank parking and official viewing stands at major venues — arrive early and confirm local transport and viewing pass details with organisers.

latest.text: The CBL 2026 season is scheduled to conclude with the President’s Trophy final at Ashtamudi Lake, Kollam on November 21, 2026 (CBL final event).
Aroma Chundan wins the Thazhathangadi round (October 24, 2026) and reappears as a strong contender on the 2026 CBL points table.
CBL Season 6 officially begins at Karuvatta (Alappuzha) on September 19, 2026, marking an 11‑race calendar across the state organised by Kerala Tourism.

visitorInfo.howToReach: Use Alappuzha as a base for most CBL races (well connected by road and rail to Kochi/Ernakulam). For the final, reach Kollam (Ashtamudi) by train or bus from Kochi or Thiruvananthapuram; confirm local transport and event parking before you go.
etiquette: Arrive early — best viewing spots fill fast and banks can be narrow.
Bring sun/rain protection; dress modestly and respect riverbank etiquette.
Use official viewing stands where available and follow steward instructions for safety.
Confirm exact race date, start time and viewing rules with Kerala Tourism or local organisers before travel.
